# An external caller triggering a node by POSTing to a route

The bundled `sensor-webhook` service turns an authenticated inbound call into a
message on a target instance, with no poll interval in between.

## Wire the sensor

```yaml
persistence:
  driver: sqlite
  sqlite:
    path: /var/lib/rimsky/state.db
claim_producers: {}
named_locks: {}
executors: {}
publishers:
  "hook-secret":
    endpoint: "webhook-sensor:9084"
    protocols: ["publisher"]
  "hook-hmac":
    endpoint: "webhook-sensor:9084"
    protocols: ["publisher"]
```

```bash
docker run -d --network rimsky-net --network-alias webhook-sensor -p 9184:9184 \
  -e RIMSKY_SENSOR_WEBHOOK_PORT=9084 \
  -e RIMSKY_SENSOR_WEBHOOK_HTTP_PORT=9184 \
  -e RIMSKY_CONTROL_API_URL=http://rimsky:8080 \
  rimsky-sensor-webhook:<tag>
```

The sensor serves its health route before any subscription exists.

## The template

Two endpoints, one per authentication form.

```json
{
  "name": "webhook-demo",
  "version": "1",
  "messages": [{"type": "hook/secret"}, {"type": "hook/hmac"}],
  "nodes": [{
    "type": "handler",
    "kind": "attribute_passthrough",
    "subscribes": [
      {"node": "hook/secret", "type": "terminal/success", "force_upstream_refresh": false},
      {"node": "hook/hmac",   "type": "terminal/success", "force_upstream_refresh": false}
    ],
    "attributes": {"schema": {"type": "object",
                              "properties": {"v": {"type": "integer", "default": 1}}}}
  }],
  "publishers": [
    {"name": "hook-secret", "kind": "webhook", "message_type": "hook/secret",
     "config": {"path_prefix": "/hooks/secret",
                "auth": {"mode": "secret_header", "header": "X-Token",
                         "secret": "<your secret>"}}},
    {"name": "hook-hmac", "kind": "webhook", "message_type": "hook/hmac",
     "config": {"path_prefix": "/hooks/hmac",
                "idempotency_header": "X-Delivery-Id",
                "auth": {"mode": "hmac", "secret": "<your secret>",
                         "timestamp_header": "X-Rimsky-Timestamp",
                         "replay_window_seconds": 60}}}
  ]
}
```

## A shared-header call

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:9184/hooks/secret" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'X-Token: <your secret>' \
  -d '{"event":"deploy"}'
# 200
```

The message is already on the target instance when the call returns. No poll
interval sits between the call and the message. The subscribed node runs on it.

A call with no header and a call with the wrong header are each refused 401, and
neither becomes a message. Refusal is complete, not partial.

## A signed call

Sign the timestamp and body with the shared secret:

```bash
TS=$(date +%s)
SIG="sha256=$(printf '%s' "$TS.$BODY" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "<your secret>" -r | cut -d' ' -f1)"

curl -sS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:9184/hooks/hmac" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -H "X-Rimsky-Timestamp: $TS" \
  -H "X-Rimsky-Signature: $SIG" \
  -H "X-Delivery-Id: delivery-1" \
  -d "$BODY"
# 200
```

Accepted, and likewise already a message when it returns, carrying its delivery
id.

A call signed with the wrong secret is refused 401. A correctly signed call
bearing a timestamp an hour old is refused 401 by the declared replay window: a
captured body cannot be replayed later even with a valid signature.

## A retried delivery does not double the work

Redeliver a body under a delivery id the sensor has already seen. The call is
accepted rather than refused, and it produces no second message.

An external system that retries on its own triggers the node once, and the
operator does not have to make the graph tolerate duplicates.

## A path no subscription declares is refused

```bash
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST \
  "http://127.0.0.1:9184/hooks/nothing" -d '{}'
# 404
```

The declared subscription is what opens a route.
